Early verification of the in-flight padding mechanism (relation-fit.R read_padded / .residual_padded_block). residual-statistics.R was 11 seconds old so I did not read it; this is only the foundation underneath.

THE TARGET PROPERTY ALREADY HOLDS. n=120, p=40, fixed width 32, reading in blocks of 8 versus 16:

  bitwise identical: TRUE, max|diff| = 0

That is exactly the guarantee this bead asks for, and the padded tail residualizes to exactly zero (max|padded tail| = 0), so zero-fill does not contaminate the statistics. The approach works.

ONE HAZARD AT THE BOUNDARY between the two readers

residual_block() reads unpadded; .residual_padded_block() residualizes the PADDED matrix and slices. Those are different GEMM shapes, so they do not always agree:

  features= 4  width= 4   bitwise TRUE   0
  features= 4  width=16   bitwise FALSE  4.44e-16
  features= 4  width=32   bitwise FALSE  4.44e-16
  features= 4  width=64   bitwise FALSE  4.44e-16
  features= 8  width=8/16/32/64  bitwise TRUE  0
  features=13  width=13/16/32/64 bitwise TRUE  0

The disagreement is shape-dependent and appears at some widths and not others - the same BLAS kernel-selection effect this bead is about, now surfacing at the padded/unpadded boundary rather than at the block boundary.

Two consequences worth deciding before the accumulator closes:

1. Metric construction should use read_padded EXCLUSIVELY. If any path inside metric estimation mixes residual_block() with padded reads, the plan-independence guarantee is silently reintroduced as a plan-dependence, because which reader is used would then matter.

2. Any test asserting that the two readers agree must use a tolerance, not identical(). A test written with identical() would pass at features=8 and 13 and fail at features=4, which reads as a flaky test rather than as the shape effect it actually is.

Neither is a defect in what you have built. Flagging now because the accumulator has no tests yet and both are cheap to settle at this stage.
